context.body: One action is described through opposed human and divine intentions.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Joseph distinguishes his brothers’ evil intention from God’s intention to preserve many lives.
observations.label: Joseph names God’s purpose in human evil: action

observations.body: The brothers fear revenge; Joseph refuses God’s place and comforts them.
observations.label: Joseph names God’s purpose in human evil: response

observations.body: Am I in the place of God? · meant evil · meant for good
observations.label: Words in Genesis 50:15–21

payload.posture: Read Genesis 50:15–21 as promise and the patriarchs evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage names God’s good purpose without calling the brothers’ evil good.
payload.title: Joseph names God’s purpose in human evil
